newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Chirac to review judicial independence.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac to review judicial independence.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Thursday he would launch a reform to review ways of strengthening the independence of the judiciary and bolster the presumption of innocence for suspects.

Chirac, asked in a television interview about sleaze probes into most political parties including his own Gaullist party, said he had instructed the government to name a commission to review the workings of French justice.

Grilled at length for the first time since he came to office in 1995 about suspected political kickbacks in France, Chirac said: "Probes must be carried out to the end and punishment must be all the more exemplary as it concerns people in position of power."

Chirac there had been a "subsidence of public morality" in France in recent years. Several officials from Paris City Hall, where Chirac was mayor until he was elected president in 1995, are targeted by probes into suspect political funding.
The government-appointed commission, including a broad range of legal experts, would also examine ways to cut out bureaucracy that means many minor crimes never reach court, Chirac said.

The commission would examine making prosecutors independent of the Justice Ministry -- prosecutors currently report to the ministry. He also said that many people suffered "a political-media hunt" that belied the principle that citizens were innocent until proven guilty.
